title: The end of the Appian Way
learning_goal: Find the base of the lost second column and the steps down to the water, and know that Rome's road east ends 150 m from the quay where Britain's mail for India was put on a ship.

narration.script:
Last stop before the sea. Two things to find. Above you, le colonne romane — the Roman columns, though only one of them is still standing. Find the other: there is a base, and nothing more. Then find the steps down to the water.

It fell in 1582; the pieces went to Lecce. This is the end of the Appian Way, Rome's road east. A hundred and fifty metres along that quay, Britain's mail for India got on a ship. And Virgil died in this town.

media.note: Piazzetta Colonne Romane, at the head of the harbour steps. The standing column (F-106, 40.64112,17.94685) bears about 078° at 9 m; the Scalinata Virgiliana runs down to the water at 049°, about 21 m; the Stazione Marittima (F-107, 40.64033,17.94843) bears about 121° at 166 m. Maps EMBED, free SKU, drag to look — nothing billable (RULE 1, D3, D6). Pano availability EXPECTED (public piazzetta); QA confirms in the player, because the studio's key is referrer-restricted. Fallback if the pano is missing: M-248 with the same task read as a tilt-up.

production_notes: SEGMENT 8, second third (50 s; 84 words). STOP-AND-LOOK #2 OF 2, and that is the D6 budget for the chapter — do not add a third. Two named finds, both said out loud, and the payoff is the chapter's closing image: Rome's road east ends 150 m from the quay where Britain's road east began. The stop's coordinates are on the M-215 media entry; no `interaction.route`, no walking. VIRGIL GETS ONE LINE AND NO MORE (the rundown's instruction) and it is deliberately last, so the scene ends on a town rather than on an argument. THE COLUMN'S HEIGHT (18.74 m, F-88) is NOT spoken — it is a caption candidate for the film; the guide says 'above you' and lets the tilt-up do it. As in scene 11, the payoff sits in `script` rather than `after_script`, because the player speaks `after_script` only for graded interactions and a `look` scene has none. Same known engine stall as Day-1 scene 15 (a `look` scene waits for ▶). LINEAR CUT (40 s): M-211 (Mapillary pano, licence unresolved — rundown Decision 4) as a slow pan right-to-left ending on the column, or M-248 as a tilt-up if the Mapillary question is answered no; either way the words are unchanged and the guide names what the player-traveller would have found.
